BLOCKER: `backlog_db_export.py --prune` deletes every projection when the DB query returns zero rows (wrong DSN, tenant typo, or RLS-bound role with no `app.tenant_id`), destroying the very files rollback depends on.
Add a hard guard: refuse to prune on `rows == 0`, require an explicit confirmation flag, and validate/prune only after a full successful read.
MAJOR: `backlog_db_parity.py` reports "OK -> safe to set on" on 0 files/0 rows (tenant typo or RLS-blocked read), producing false-green AC-3 evidence; it should fail when both sides are empty or when the tenant is not in `PF_BACKLOG_DB_SCOPES`.

`Get`/`List`/`Delete` trust only `current_setting('app.tenant_id')` and never cross-check the requested tenant (unlike `Put`); a session-scoped GUC leak on a pooled connection yields cross-tenant reads that RLS also permits. Compare the bound tenant with the requested tenant or assert transaction-local binding.

0021 is one-way in practice: `down` refuses once legacy cross-tenant duplicates exist, the new binary requires 0021 at `Authority()`, and the old binary's `ON CONFLICT (id)` is invalid — so only the flag can be rolled back. Document this as forward-fix-only or provide a compatible write path.

`_load_all_from_db` hardcodes `limit=100000` with no pagination and 0022 adds no `(tenant_id, created_at DESC)` index behind `List ... ORDER BY created_at DESC`; silent truncation and p95 SLO risk grow with tenant size.

Precheck forcing `PF_BACKLOG_DB=off` makes the new `functional-spec`/`spec-pack`/`conformance` gates evaluate derived, possibly stale file projections rather than DB authority, with no freshness/parity precondition — frozen-SHA gate results can be wrong.
MINOR: `delete()` omits the `"product_forge"` default used by `_save_item` (`str(project or scope or "")`), so an item with neither field is saved to the DB tenant but deleted via the file path, leaving orphan DB rows.

`go/edpsvc` maps `ErrTenantContext` to 503, which `_load_all_from_db` collapses into `BACKLOG_DB_UNAVAILABLE`; a tenant-context misconfiguration is indistinguishable from an outage in logs and alerts.

`backlog_migration_preflight.py` checks `contype='u'` (excludes the pkey, so `unknown_uniques` can never fire), only prints `pg_indexes`, and accepts any existing `PF_BACKUP_ARTIFACT` file without size/recency validation.
`backlog_db_backfill.py --tenant` bypasses the `_db_for` allowlist check, so a non-allowlisted tenant fails per item via `store_item_to_db` instead of being skipped cleanly.
Enforcement dates disagree: `config/functional-spec.json` and `config/spec-pack.json` use `2026-11-07` while `docs/SPEC-CHAIN.md` binds items from `2026-11-06`.
NIT: `_has_placeholder` is a raw substring scan over "todo"/"tbd"/"unspecified", so it both misses "T.B.D." and false-positives on ordinary prose; use word-boundary matching on enforced fields.
`functional_spec.fresh()`/`spec_pack.fresh()` compare only `split("\n", 2)[-1]`, so drift in the title/version header is never detected.
`gate1_check` passes `{}` when the item is not found and every `problems({})` returns `[]`, so a missing item silently passes the new spec-chain gates.
SUMMARY: Direction is correct (default-on with scoped allowlist, tenant-scoped Go access, ordered migrations), but the rollback path is unsafe: export/prune can wipe the file projections it is meant to reconstruct, and parity can green-light an empty comparison.
Tenant isolation rests entirely on the transaction-local GUC for read/delete; add a requested-tenant cross-check before calling AC-4 satisfied.

Schema/binary rollback is effectively one-way once legacy duplicates exist; state that explicitly and back it with a test, and add the missing `(tenant_id, created_at)` index plus pagination for `List`.
